messages:
Maya: Ok team — starting a PRD intake thread for an "initiative gating" playbook we can use when customers ask for custom acceptance gates (example: ACME wants per-tenant quality thresholds + canary rules). Goal is a thin, repeatable checklist + acceptance criteria template.
Sam: +1, we need something we can hand to sales/SEs to set expectations early.
Alex: Quick Q — do we mean gating during rollout (canary + auto-rollback) or gating at runtime (reject responses below threshold)? both?
Maya: Prefer rollout gating primarily (canary, step-rollout, auto-fallback). Runtime gating (rejecting responses) is a potential future add-on — mark as non-goal for initial phase.
Jamie: For acceptance criteria we should include measurable eval sets, latency/regression budgets, and failover behavior. Eg: "no more than X% regressions on A/B evals, <Yms p95 increase".
Priya: From sales: ACME will expect documented metrics and a rollback window (they asked for 15-minute max exposure). They also want an audit log of decisions.
Alex: Noted. Implementation constraints: Dedicated + Hosted pipelines differ. Need a config model that maps a tenant -> rollout policy + eval set + metric thresholds.
Maya: Sketch of the problem statement (short): customers want predictable quality during rollouts for tenant-sensitive workloads. We lack a standardized intake + PRD template to capture goals/non-goals/metrics/edge cases.
Sam: Proposed success metrics (draft):
```
- Number of intake->prod rollouts using the template (target 10 in Q2)
- Reduction in manual rollback incidents by 30% for gated rollouts
- Time to reach decision during canary reduced to < 20m
```

Alex: Acceptance criteria draft (suggested):
```
- Template exists and is used for >=2 pilot customers
- Canary automation will pause traffic and surface a single pass/fail signal based on eval set
- If evaluation fails, system triggers configured fallback within 15m
- All gated rollouts produce audit logs stored for 90d
- No p95 latency regressions > 20% during canary window
```

Jamie: Edge cases to capture: customers with very small eval sets, tenants that share models (cross-tenant noise), and synthetic traffic that distorts metrics. Also network partition during canary.
Priya: Customer ask: per-tenant thresholds need an override path (SE approval) — will that live in Console or config file? customers expect Console visibility.
Alex: Console UI visibility is a follow-up, but we can expose policy metadata in API + telemetry first. Mark UI as stretch.
Maya: Non-goals (initial): runtime rejection/response-level gating, full Console UI, multi-region coordinated rollouts.
Sam: Implementation notes: keep policy DSL tiny: {policy_id, eval_suite_id, threshold_map, rollback_window_minutes, fallback_model_id}.
Alex: Technical risk: building eval-suite infra + attaching to canary runner. Could reuse existing eval harness but need faster short-running evals for canaries.
Priya: I'll line up 2 pilot customers (ACME + BetaCo) and get their sample eval sets this week.
Maya: Next steps: Sam to turn this into a one-page PRD + checklist; Alex to draft the minimal policy schema; Priya to collect pilot data; Jamie to enumerate edge-case tests.
Sam: I'll drop a PRD draft by EOD Thursday and ping this thread.
DeployBot: Deploy pipeline notice: canary-runner v0.9 deployed to staging at 2412345701.
Alex: Thanks — will start integration tests against staging canary-runner once PRD lands.
Maya: Awesome. If anyone spots missing success metrics or acceptance items call them out here. :thumbsup:
